payers.accessNotes: All five policies below were retrieved in FULL as live HTML from aetna.com on 2026-08-30 and read directly; nothing here is reconstructed from memory. IMPORTANT ACCESS DETAIL: WebFetch returned HTTP 403 on every aetna.com URL (bot-block). The documents were successfully retrieved via curl with a desktop browser User-Agent (HTTP 200) and converted to text locally. The public CPB pages are the SAME documents Aetna publishes for providers. LIMITS / WHAT IS NOT HERE: (1) Aetna's public CPBs are the plan-agnostic clinical criteria only - they do NOT include the Aetna Medicare Advantage supplemental criteria, the plan-specific precertification lists, or the internal reviewer worksheets; whether a given CPT actually requires precert must be checked in Aetna's CPT code search tool, which was NOT retrieved. (2) The CPT/ICD-10 code tables in these CPBs are very long; the code arrays below are the codes ACTUALLY listed under each named section heading in the source table, but for several sections Aetna prints 'Codes not listed due to expanded specificity' and for ICD-10 'not all inclusive' - so the ICD-10 lists are NOT exhaustive and are marked as such. (3) Aetna's 'Background' and 'References' sections were retrieved but not encoded here (they are evidence narrative, not criteria). (4) No Aetna policy retrieved states an ODI/NDI or other numeric functional-outcome-score threshold for fusion or decompression; the only numeric pain/function thresholds found anywhere are VAS>5 for lumbar disc arthroplasty (CPB 0591) and NRS>=5 baseline plus >=70% injection response for SI joint fusion (CPB 0016). Do not infer an ODI requirement for Aetna - there is none in the published text. (5) Aetna does NOT require EMG/NCS, psychological clearance, or a BMI threshold anywhere in these policies. Bone density (DEXA) is required only for cervical disc arthroplasty in members 60+ and is an exclusion criterion for lumbar disc arthroplasty. There is no BMI/obesity criterion at all - do not add one.

procedures.procedure: lumbar spinal fusion with osteotomy / lordotic anterior interbody implants
procedures.indication: iatrogenic or degenerative flatback syndrome with significant sagittal imbalance

requirements.requirement: Standing radiographs of the spine must show significant sagittal imbalance, defined as ANY of: offset greater than 5 cm between the sagittal vertebral axis (plumb line from center of C7 body) and the posterior superior aspect of S1; OR pelvic tilt greater than 20 degrees; OR lumbar lordosis to pelvic incidence mismatch greater than or equal to 10 degrees.
requirements.verbatimQuote: sagittal imbalance on standing radiographs of the spine are considered significant where there is: an offset of greater than 5 cm between the sagittal vertebral axis (a plumb line downward from the center of the C7 vertebral body) and the posterior superior aspect of the S1 vertebral body; or a pelvic tilt greater than 20 degrees; or a lumbar lordosis to pelvic incidence mismatch of greater than or equal to 10 degrees

requirements.requirement: Flatback syndrome defined as back pain, stooped posture and limitation of forward gaze.
requirements.verbatimQuote: Iatrogenic or degenerative flatback syndrome (defined as members with back pain, stooped posture and limitation of forward gaze)

requirements.requirement: Failed 3 months of conservative management, unless a waiver condition applies.

exclusions: Fusion must be performed WITH spinal osteotomy and/or lordotic anterior interbody implants sufficient to restore anterior height and lordosis.

procedures.indication: spinal fracture / dislocation with instability or neural element compromise

requirements.requirement: Spinal fracture causing instability or neural element compromise/compression, spinal dislocation with mechanical instability, locked facets, or fracture with displaced fragment confirmed by ADVANCED imaging (CT or MRI) causing neural element compromise.
requirements.verbatimQuote: Spinal fracture causing instability or neural element compromise/compression, spinal dislocation (associated with mechanical instability), locked facets, or fracture with displaced fracture fragment confirmed by advanced imaging studies (CT or MRI) causing neural element compromise, which may be combined with a laminectomy.

exclusions: Pars defects/pars fractures
Subacute or chronic compression fractures
Compression fractures without retropulsion that is causing significant canal stenosis
Chronic stable odontoid fractures
Spinous process fractures
Transverse process fractures
Stable isolated pedicle fractures

procedures.indication: pars defect (fracture) without significant instability, in members under 18

requirements.requirement: Members under 18 years of age with pars defect and disc degeneration at the surgical level must have failed at least 6 MONTHS of conservative management that includes bracing AND at least 6 weeks of formal in-person physical therapy within the past year.
requirements.durationRequired: at least 6 months conservative management; at least 6 weeks formal in-person PT within the past year
requirements.verbatimQuote: Pars defects (fractures) without significant instability (for spondylolisthesis/instability follow criteria (9) below) and with disc degeneration at the surgical level in members under 18 years of age who have failed at least 6 months of conservative management that includes bracing and at least 6 weeks of formal in-person physical therapy within the past year. If there is no disc degeneration then pars repair is appropriate

requirements.requirement: Conservative management must include bracing.
requirements.verbatimQuote: conservative management that includes bracing

exclusions: This pathway applies only to members UNDER 18 years of age - it is not available to adults.
If there is no disc degeneration, pars repair (not fusion) is appropriate.

requirements.requirement: Spinal surgery in persons with prior spinal surgery is medically necessary when any of the criteria in Sections I.A. through I.E. are met.
requirements.verbatimQuote: Spinal surgery in persons with prior spinal surgery when any of the above criteria (I.A. through I.E.) are met

requirements.requirement: For severe back or neck pain after the fusion has healed related to the spinal instrumentation: must have failed conservative management including at least 6 weeks of formal IN-PERSON physical therapy in the past year.
requirements.durationRequired: at least 6 weeks in the past year
requirements.verbatimQuote: Severe back or neck pain after the fusion has healed related to the spinal instrumentation that has failed conservative management, including at least 6 weeks of formal in-person physical therapy in the past year

requirements.requirement: Alternative pathway: neurologic complication related to the ongoing presence of the instrumentation (e.g., a screw compressing a nerve root causing radiculopathy).
requirements.verbatimQuote: Neurologic complication related to the ongoing presence of the instrumentation (e.g., a screw is compressing a nerve root causing radiculopathy)

requirements.requirement: Alternative pathways: symptomatic rod, hook, or screw migration, dislodgment, or breakage; new pain or protruding mass at operative site after significant spinal trauma; vascular complications; spinal infection; or further approved surgery requiring removal.

exclusions: Not reimbursable when new instrumentation is inserted at levels including all or part of the previously instrumented segments - considered integral to the procedure.

requirements.requirement: Any of: further approved surgery requiring removal; neurologic or vascular complication from the instrumentation; instrumentation failure/migration that could cause neurologic or vascular complications; spinal infection; or dysphagia related to esophageal compression by anterior cervical implants CONFIRMED BY ENT EVALUATION OR BARIUM SWALLOW STUDY.
requirements.verbatimQuote: Dysphagia related to esophageal compression by anterior cervical implants (confirmed by ENT evaluation or barium swallow study)

exclusions: Not reimbursable when new instrumentation is inserted at levels including all or part of the previously instrumented segments.

procedures.indication: long fusion to sacrum, non-union, sacral insufficiency fracture, high-grade L5/S1 spondylolisthesis

requirements.requirement: Criteria for lumbar fusion must be met, AND any of: requested fusion from L2 or above to the sacrum; a multi-level fusion with non-union or sacral insufficiency fracture; or fusion of a high grade lumbosacral spondylolisthesis at L5/S1 (Grade 3 or more).
requirements.verbatimQuote: Pelvic fixation is considered medically necessary where criteria for lumbar fusion (in I.1.9) are met, for any of the following: With a requested fusion from L2 or above to the sacrum; or A multi-level fusion with non-union or sacral insufficiency fracture; or Fusion of a high grade lumbosacral spondylolisthesis at L5/S1 (Grade 3 or more)

requirements.requirement: Approvable only if fusion implants are being placed, and documentation includes identification of the stereotaxic system used, registration and review of imaging data sets with verification of accuracy, and intraoperative use of the navigation system.
requirements.verbatimQuote: Computer-assisted surgical navigation (stereotaxic navigation) is approvable if fusion implants are being placed during surgery on the spinal column when identification of the stereotaxic system being used, registration and review of imaging data sets with verification of accuracy and intraoperative use of the navigation system is documented. Computer-assisted surgical navigation is not approvable during routine decompression surgery. Exceptions may be for decompressions for tumor.

exclusions: Not approvable during routine decompression surgery (exceptions may be for decompressions for tumor).
Computer-assisted surgical navigation for laminectomies is experimental, investigational, or unproven.
Robotic assistance is considered integral to the primary procedure and not separately reimbursed.

procedures.indication: symptomatic cervical degenerative disc disease or herniated disc at 1 level, or 2 contiguous levels for specified devices

requirements.requirement: One level, C3 to C7, with an FDA-approved device and device-specific age limits. Two contiguous levels permitted only for Mobi-C (21-67), Prestige LP (21-78), Simplify (<70), Prodisc-C Vivo and Prodisc-C SK (18 to <70).
requirements.verbatimQuote: Or at 2 contiguous levels (also see Additional Notes section): Mobi-C and member is at least 21 years and not older than 67 years of age; Prestige LP Cervical Disc and member is at least 21 years and not older than 78 years of age; Simplify Cervical Artificial Disc and member is less than 70 years of age; Prodisc-C Vivo and Prodisc-C SK and member is at least 18 years and less than 70 years of age.

requirements.requirement: All other reasonable sources of pain and/or neurological deficit ruled out; CT or MRI shows nerve root or spinal cord compression at the corresponding level, OR central/lateral recess or foraminal stenosis graded moderate, moderate-to-severe or severe (not mild or mild-to-moderate).
requirements.verbatimQuote: Imaging studies (e.g., CT or MRI) indicate: Nerve root or spinal cord compression at the level corresponding with the clinical findings; or Central/lateral recess or foraminal stenosis graded as moderate, moderate to severe or severe (not mild or mild to moderate)

requirements.requirement: Signs or symptoms of neural compression (radiculopathy, neurogenic claudication, myelopathy) associated with the levels being treated.
requirements.verbatimQuote: Member has signs or symptoms of neural compression (radiculopathy, neurogenic claudication, myelopathy) associated with the levels being treated

requirements.requirement: There must be NO radiologic evidence of segmental instability. Instability is a CONTRAINDICATION for arthroplasty (unlike fusion, where it is an indication).
requirements.verbatimQuote: There is no radiologic evidence of segmental instability

requirements.requirement: Failed at least 6 weeks of conservative therapy; PT must be in-person (not home or virtual) and span the entire 6 weeks; confirmed by PT notes or claims history.
requirements.verbatimQuote: Member has failed at least 6 weeks of conservative therapy (see Note below for details and reasons to waive conservative treatment)

requirements.requirement: Conservative measures must include patient education; active in-person PT; medications (NSAIDs, acetaminophen, or tricyclic antidepressants); and where appropriate identification and management of associated anxiety and depression. Must be recent (within the past year).
requirements.verbatimQuote: Conservative measures must be recent (within the past year) and include the following non-surgical measures and medications unless one or more of the requirements for waiver below are met: patient education; active physical therapy (in-person as opposed to home or virtual physical therapy); medications (NSAIDS, acetaminophen, or tricyclic antidepressants), and (where appropriate) identification and management of associated anxiety and depression.

requirements.requirement: Member's activities of daily living are limited by symptoms of neural compression.
requirements.verbatimQuote: Member's activities of daily living are limited by symptoms of neural compression

requirements.requirement: Member must not have a diagnosis of osteoporosis or osteopenia. For members 60 YEARS OF AGE AND OLDER, a DEXA scan confirming a T score of -1.0 or higher WITHIN THE PAST YEAR is required.
requirements.verbatimQuote: Member does not have a diagnosis of osteoporosis or osteopenia, and for members 60 years of age and older, member had a DEXA scan confirming T score of - 1.0 or higher within the past year.

exclusions: Artificial cervical discs are experimental, investigational, or unproven for persons with prior disc replacement if the new request would result in more than 2 contiguous disc replacement levels from C3 to C7.
M6-C Artificial Cervical Disc is experimental, investigational, or unproven.
Radiologic evidence of segmental instability disqualifies.
Osteoporosis or osteopenia disqualifies.

procedures.indication: lumbar degenerative disc disease, single level L3-4, L4-L5 or L5-S1

requirements.requirement: Single level only, at L3-4, L4-L5 or L5-S1, per FDA approved indications. Age 18 to 60.
requirements.verbatimQuote: Age limitations: 18 to 60 years ... Degenerative disease is at single level at L3-4, L4-L5 or L5-S1 per FDA approved indications

requirements.requirement: Significant level of pain: VAS greater than 5.
requirements.verbatimQuote: Significant level of pain (VAS greater than 5)

requirements.requirement: Clinically significant functional impairment. NOTE: Aetna does NOT specify a numeric ODI threshold.
requirements.verbatimQuote: Clinically significant functional impairment

requirements.requirement: Failure of SIX OR MORE MONTHS of physician-supervised multi-modal conservative management for functionally disabling mechanical low back pain, including at least 3 MONTHS of in-person (not virtual) formal PT in the past year.
requirements.durationRequired: six or more months of conservative management; at least 3 months of in-person formal PT in the past year
requirements.verbatimQuote: Failure of six or more months of physician-supervised multi-modal conservative management for functionally disabling mechanical low back pain, including analgesics and at least 3 months of in-person (not virtual) formal PT in the past year

requirements.requirement: Conservative management must include analgesics.
requirements.verbatimQuote: including analgesics

requirements.requirement: Single level disease confirmed by a RECENT (within 6 months) x-ray AND MRI or CT.
requirements.verbatimQuote: Single level disease has been confirmed by a recent (within 6 months) x-ray and MRI or CT

requirements.requirement: MRI or CT within 6 months confirming single-level disease and excluding the listed contraindications.
requirements.verbatimQuote: Single level disease has been confirmed by a recent (within 6 months) x-ray and MRI or CT

requirements.requirement: No osteopenia or osteoporosis (T-score less than -1.0 disqualifies).
requirements.verbatimQuote: No osteopenia or osteoporosis (T-score less than -1.0)

requirements.requirement: Absence of unmanaged significant mental and/or behavioral health disorders (e.g., major depressive disorder, chronic pain syndrome, secondary gain, opioid and alcohol use disorders).
requirements.verbatimQuote: Absence of unmanaged significant mental and/or behavioral health disorders (e.g., major depressive disorder, chronic pain syndrome, secondary gain, opioid and alcohol use disorders).

requirements.requirement: No prior destabilizing spine surgery of any form at the target level.
requirements.verbatimQuote: No prior destabilizing spine surgery of any form at the target level

exclusions: Degenerative or lytic spondylolisthesis greater than 3mm
Lumbar spinal stenosis (at least moderate central stenosis)
Pars interarticularis defect with either spondylolysis or isthmic spondylolisthesis
Lumbar scoliosis (greater than 11 degrees of coronal plane deformity)
Spinal fracture
Infection
Symptomatic degenerative disc disease at more than one level
Facet ankylosis or severe facet degeneration at the operative level
Presence of tumor or active infection at the site of implantation
Lumbar nerve root compression or bony spinal stenosis (nerve root compression or at least moderate lateral recess or foraminal stenosis)
Preoperative remaining disc height of less than 2 mm
Mid-sagittal stenosis of less than 8 mm (by MRI) with symptomatic neurogenic claudication
No use in combination with a spinal fusion
No use in combination with a lumbar stabilization procedure
Vertebral bodies at the affected level compromised from trauma
Ankylosing spondylitis, rheumatoid arthritis, lupus, or other autoimmune disorder
Allergy or sensitivity to implant materials
Isolated radicular compression syndromes due to lumbar disc herniation or bony stenosis
Vascular, urological, or other peritoneal or retroperitoneal pathology precluding safe anterior exposure
Lumbar prosthetic intervertebral discs at more than one level are experimental, investigational, or unproven
Lumbar partial disc prosthetics (e.g., Nubac, DASCOR Disc Arthroplasty System) are experimental, investigational, or unproven
MOTUS lumbar total joint replacement / posterior vertebral joint replacement (3Spine) is experimental, investigational, or unproven
Total posterior spine (TOPS) System is experimental, investigational, or unproven
Three-dimensional (3D) bioprinting for intervertebral disc regeneration is experimental, investigational, or unproven

procedures.procedure: minimally invasive sacroiliac joint fusion (transfixing, e.g. iFuse)
procedures.indication: sacroiliac joint syndrome interfering with activities of daily living

requirements.requirement: Adults 18 years of age or older with sacroiliac joint pain for GREATER THAN 6 MONTHS (or greater than 18 months for pregnancy-induced pelvic girdle pain).
requirements.durationRequired: greater than 6 months (greater than 18 months for pregnancy-induced pelvic girdle pain)
requirements.verbatimQuote: Adults 18 years of age or older with sacroiliac joint (SIJ) pain for greater than 6 months (or greater than 18 months for pregnancy induced pelvic girdle pain)

requirements.requirement: Pain at or close to the posterior superior iliac spine (PSIS) with possible radiation into buttocks, posterior thigh, or groin, and the member can point to the location of pain (Fortin Finger Test). Baseline lower back pain score of at least 5 on a 0-10 point NRS.
requirements.verbatimQuote: Member has pain at or close to the posterior superior iliac spine (PSIS) with possible radiation into buttocks, posterior thigh, or groin and can point to the location of pain (Fortin Finger Test) ... Baseline lower back pain score of at least 5 on 0-10 point NRS

requirements.requirement: At least 3 of 5 physical examination maneuvers specific for SI joint pain must be positive: Compression; Posterior Pelvic Pain Provocation test - P4 (Thigh Thrust); Patrick's test (Fabere); Sacroiliac distraction test; Gaenslen's test.
requirements.verbatimQuote: Member has at least 3 of 5 physical examination maneuvers specific for SI joint pain: Compression; Posterior Pelvic Pain Provocation test - P4 (Thigh Thrust); Patrick's test (Fabere); Sacroiliac distraction test; Gaenslen's test

requirements.requirement: Recent (within 6 months) imaging must include plain X-rays and/or cross-sectional imaging (CT or MRI) of the pelvis excluding destructive lesions, acute fracture or inflammatory arthropathy; AND plain X-rays of the pelvis including the ipsilateral hip to exclude concomitant hip pathology.
requirements.verbatimQuote: Member has had recent (within 6 months) diagnostic imaging studies that include all of the following: Plain X-rays and/or cross sectional imaging of the pelvis (CT or MRI) that excludes the presence of destructive lesions (e.g. tumor, infection), acute fracture or inflammatory arthropathy that would not be properly addressed by SIJ fusion; and Plain X-rays of the pelvis including the ipsilateral hip to exclude potential concomitant hip pathology

requirements.requirement: Cross-sectional imaging (CT or MRI) of the LUMBAR SPINE to exclude potential concomitant neural compression or other degenerative conditions. Plus radiologic evidence of SI joint degeneration on imaging.
requirements.verbatimQuote: Cross-sectional imaging (e.g. CT or MRI) of the lumbar spine to exclude potential concomitant neural compression or other degenerative conditions ... Radiologic evidence of SI joint degeneration on imaging

requirements.requirement: At least 70% improvement in lower back pain NRS from pre-injection score after TWO SEPARATE fluoroscopic or CT controlled injections of local anesthetic into the affected SI joint within the past year, and at least one injection must be therapeutic and include a steroid. The injections must have been ISOLATED to only the SI joint - if combined with hip, trochanteric bursa, or lumbar spine injections at the same time they do NOT count.
requirements.verbatimQuote: Member has improvement in lower back pain numeric rating scale (NRS) of at least 70% of the pre injection NRS score after two separate fluoroscopic or CT controlled injection of local anesthetic (and at least one injection must be therapeutic and include a steroid) into affected SI joint within the past year. These injections must have been isolated to only the SI joint, so if they were combined with other injections at the same time (e.g., hip, trochanteric bursa, or lumbar spine) they could not be used to meet this criterion

requirements.requirement: Clinician must document that other neighboring motion segments have been evaluated and ruled out as potential pain generators, including diagnostic testing with facet/medial branch blocks and/or interlaminar epidural injections as appropriate based on the member's presentation.
requirements.verbatimQuote: Clinician has documented that other neighboring motion segments have been evaluated and ruled out as potential pain generators, including diagnostic testing with facet/medial branch blocks and or interlaminar epidural injections, as appropriate based on the member's presentation

requirements.requirement: Interlaminar epidural injections may be required as part of ruling out neighboring motion segments as pain generators.
requirements.verbatimQuote: including diagnostic testing with facet/medial branch blocks and or interlaminar epidural injections, as appropriate based on the member's presentation

requirements.requirement: 6 MONTHS of adequate conservative treatment with little or no response, including pharmacotherapy (e.g., NSAIDs), activity modification, and AT LEAST THREE MONTHS of formal in-person physical therapy in the past year.
requirements.durationRequired: 6 months conservative treatment; at least 3 months formal in-person PT in the past year
requirements.verbatimQuote: Member should have tried 6 months of adequate forms of conservative treatment with little or no response, including pharmacotherapy (e.g., NSAIDS), activity modification, and at least three months of formal in-person physical therapy in the past year

requirements.requirement: Pharmacotherapy (e.g., NSAIDs) and activity modification required.

Member should be nicotine-free for AT LEAST 1 YEAR prior to surgery. For persons with recent nicotine use, documentation must include a LAB REPORT (not surgeon summary) showing blood or urinary nicotine <=10 ng/ml (or urinary cotinine <=10 ng/ml) drawn within 6 weeks prior to surgery.
requirements.verbatimQuote: Member should be nicotine-free (including smoking, use of tobacco products, and nicotine replacement therapy) for at least 1 year prior to surgery. For persons with recent nicotine use, documentation of nicotine cessation should include a lab report (not surgeon summary) showing blood or urinary nicotine level of less than or equal to 10 ng/ml (or urinary cotinine levels of less than or equal to 10 ng/ml) drawn within 6 weeks prior to surgery.

requirements.requirement: SI joint syndrome must be interfering with activities of daily living.
requirements.verbatimQuote: medically necessary for sacroiliac joint syndrome interfering with activities of daily living

exclusions: Other causes of low back pain must be ruled out, including lumbar disc degeneration, lumbar disc herniation, lumbar spondylolisthesis, lumbar spinal stenosis, lumbar facet degeneration, and lumbar vertebral body fracture.
Sacroiliac pathology caused by autoimmune disease (e.g. ankylosing spondylitis), neoplasia (benign or malignant tumor), or crystal arthropathy is excluded.
Member must not have generalized pain behavior (e.g., somatoform disorder) or generalized pain disorders (e.g. fibromyalgia).
Posterior non-transfixing sacroiliac joint fixations, and use of additional joint implants with a transfixing device ('hybrid' fusions), are experimental, investigational or unproven.
Sacroiliac joint fusions are experimental, investigational, or unproven for all other indications.

procedures.indication: sacroiliac joint infection, tumor involving the sacrum, or SI pain due to severe traumatic injury

requirements.requirement: For SI pain due to severe traumatic injury, a trial of an external fixator must have been successful in providing pain relief.
requirements.verbatimQuote: Open sacroiliac joint fusion is considered medically necessary for sacroiliac joint infection, tumor involving the sacrum, and sacroiliac pain due to severe traumatic injury where a trial of an external fixator is successful in providing pain relief.

requirements.requirement: Pain must be radicular in nature. In low back pain, radicular means pain and/or numbness that radiates BELOW THE KNEE; in neck pain, pain, numbness or weakness in the shoulder, arm, wrist, or hand.
requirements.verbatimQuote: Pain is radicular in nature (radicular signs may include, but are not limited to, a positive straight leg raise or a dermatomal pattern of sensory loss). Note: In low back pain, radicular means pain and/or numbness that radiates below the knee; in neck pain, it is pain, numbness or weakness in the shoulder, arm, wrist, or hand

requirements.requirement: Intraspinal tumor or other space-occupying lesion, or non-spinal origin for pain, must be ruled out. Advanced diagnostic imaging should be performed within 24 months prior to initiating interlaminar epidural injections.
requirements.verbatimQuote: Where indicated for evaluating lumbar, cervical or thoracic pain, advanced diagnostic imaging should be performed within 24 months prior to initiating intralaminar epidural injections

requirements.requirement: Failed to improve after 4 OR MORE WEEKS of conservative treatments (e.g., rest, systemic analgesics, physical therapy).
requirements.verbatimQuote: Member has failed to improve after 4 or more weeks of conservative treatments (e.g., rest, systemic analgesics, physical therapy)

requirements.requirement: Repeat/additional ESI requires the initial injection to have produced at least 2 of: >=50% relief in pain; increase in level of function/physical activity; reduction in use of pain medication and/or additional medical services - each for at least two weeks. Limits: no more than one interlaminar ESI per session; no repeats more frequently than every two weeks; up to 3 per region per episode of pain in 6 months; up to 4 per region (cervical, thoracic, lumbar) per rolling 12-month period.
requirements.verbatimQuote: A total of up to 3 interlaminar epidural injections per region, per episode of pain are considered medically necessary in 6 months, and up to four interlaminar epidural steroid injections per region (ie, cervical, thoracic, lumbar) per rolling 12-month period are considered medically necessary, only upon return of pain and/or deterioration in function and only when responsiveness to prior injections has occurred (ie, the individual should have at least a 50% reduction in pain and/or symptoms for two weeks).

exclusions: Experimental, investigational, or unproven for non-specific low back pain and failed back syndrome.
Ultrasound guidance of epidural injections is experimental, investigational, or unproven.
More than one interlaminar epidural injection in a single region per session is not medically necessary; injection of more than one region per session is not medically necessary.

procedures.procedure: facet joint injection / medial branch block (diagnostic)
procedures.indication: facet joint syndrome, cervical C2-3 through lumbar L5-S1

requirements.requirement: Pain has lasted more than 3 months.
requirements.verbatimQuote: Pain has lasted more than 3 months

requirements.requirement: Symptoms suggestive of facet joint syndrome: absence of radiculopathy, pain aggravated by extension, rotation or lateral bending of the spine, not typically associated with neurological deficits. Facet-mediated pain confirmed by provocative testing on physical examination.
requirements.verbatimQuote: Member has symptoms suggestive of facet joint syndrome (symptoms of facet joint syndrome include absence of radiculopathy, pain that is aggravated by extension, rotation or lateral bending of the spine and is not typically associated with any neurological deficits); and Facet mediated pain is confirmed by provocative testing on physical examination (to confirm that pain is exacerbated by extension and rotation)

requirements.requirement: Pain has persisted despite SIX OR MORE WEEKS of conservative treatment (including systemic medications and/or physical therapy).
requirements.verbatimQuote: Pain has persisted despite six or more weeks of conservative treatment (including, systemic medications, and/or physical therapy)

requirements.requirement: Diagnostic facet injection is ONLY medically necessary when radiofrequency facet neurolysis is being considered. A second diagnostic injection requires the first to have produced 80% relief of facet-mediated pain for at least the expected minimum duration of the local anesthetic. No more than 3 facet joint levels per session (up to 6 injections if bilateral).
requirements.verbatimQuote: Aetna considers diagnostic facet joint injections not medically necessary where radiofrequency facet neurolysis is not being considered.

requirements.requirement: Pain limits daily activities.
requirements.verbatimQuote: Pain limits daily activities

exclusions: Diagnostic facet joint injections are experimental, investigational, or unproven for neck and back pain with UNTREATED radiculopathy.
Facet joint injections are experimental, investigational, or unproven as THERAPY for back and neck pain.
Additional sets of facet injections or medial branch blocks at the same levels and side are experimental, investigational, or unproven.
Ultrasound guidance of facet injections is experimental, investigational, or unproven.

procedures.indication: intractable cervical or back pain with or without sciatica

requirements.requirement: Severe pain limiting activities of daily living for AT LEAST 6 MONTHS.
requirements.verbatimQuote: Member has experienced severe pain limiting activities of daily living for at least 6 months

requirements.requirement: No prior spinal fusion surgery at the level to be treated.
requirements.verbatimQuote: Member has had no prior spinal fusion surgery at the level to be treated

requirements.requirement: Neuroradiologic studies are negative or fail to confirm disc herniation; no significant narrowing of the vertebral canal or spinal instability requiring surgery.
requirements.verbatimQuote: Neuroradiologic studies are negative or fail to confirm disc herniation; and Member has no significant narrowing of the vertebral canal or spinal instability requiring surgery

requirements.requirement: Tried and failed SIX OR MORE WEEKS of conservative treatments such as bed rest, back supports, physiotherapy, correction of postural abnormality, and pharmacotherapies.
requirements.verbatimQuote: Member has tried and failed six or more weeks of conservative treatments such as bed rest, back supports, physiotherapy, correction of postural abnormality, as well as pharmacotherapies (e.g., anti-inflammatory agents, analgesics, and muscle relaxants)

requirements.requirement: TWO positive diagnostic facet joint injections (intraarticular or medial branch blocks) at the level to be treated, each evidenced by at least 80% relief of facet-mediated pain for at least the expected minimum duration of the local anesthetic used.
requirements.verbatimQuote: The member has two positive diagnostic facet joint injections (intraarticular or medial branch blocks) at the level to be treated, as evidenced by at least 80% relief of facet mediated pain for at least the expected minimum duration of the effect of the local anesthetic used.

requirements.requirement: No more than three levels per session. Repeat RFA requires >50% pain relief for at least twelve weeks; further procedures at intervals of at least six months per level per side, maximum twice per rolling calendar year, only 1 treatment per level per side in a 6-month period.
requirements.verbatimQuote: Provided that greater than 50% pain relief is obtained for at least twelve weeks, further facet denervation procedures should be at intervals of at least six months per level per side, at a maximum of twice per rolling calendar year. Only 1 treatment procedure per level per side is considered medically necessary in a 6-month period.

exclusions: Radiofrequency denervation for SACROILIAC joint pain is experimental, investigational, or unproven (listed in the CPB 0016 experimental section).
Non-pulsed radiofrequency facet denervation is experimental, investigational, or unproven for all other indications.

requirements.requirement: Member has sacroiliac joint pain for greater than 3 months.
requirements.verbatimQuote: Member has sacroiliac joint (SIJ) pain for greater than 3 months

requirements.requirement: Up to 2 therapeutic/diagnostic SI injections to diagnose pain and achieve therapeutic effect; not more frequently than once every 7 days. Additional therapeutic SI injections require improvement in lower back pain NRS of at least 70% of the pre-injection score after fluoroscopic or CT controlled injection. Once diagnosis established, up to four therapeutic SI injections per 12 months, no more frequently than every 7 days.
requirements.verbatimQuote: Up to 2 therapeutic / diagnostic sacroiliac injections are considered medically necessary to diagnose the member's pain and achieve a therapeutic effect. It is not considered medically necessary to repeat these therapeutic / diagnostic injections more frequently than once every 7 days.

exclusions: Ultrasound guidance of sacroiliac joint injections is not medically necessary.
Sacroiliac ligament injection for the treatment of unspecified dorsalgia is experimental, investigational, or unproven.

procedures.procedure: intervertebral body fusion devices (cages / spacers) and spinal fixation

requirements.requirement: Cages/spacers with allograft or autogenous bone graft are medically necessary for members who meet criteria for lumbar or thoracic fusion per CPB 0743. For CERVICAL fusion, a synthetic cage/spacer requires one of: cervical corpectomy (for tumor, >50% compression fracture, retropulsed bone fragments, or symptomatic central canal stenosis from vertebral body pathology); cervical fusion for pseudarthrosis with prior fusion; or adjacent level disease in a person with a prior cervical fusion involving a plate, to avoid dissection for plate removal when a stand-alone cage/spacer is used.
requirements.verbatimQuote: Spine cages are otherwise not considered medically necessary for cervical fusion because they have not been proven more effective than bone graft for this indication.

requirements.requirement: Expandable cages are medically necessary for members meeting CPB 0743 fusion criteria AND either at L2-S1, OR for members with osseous defects at the fusion site (voids or gaps in bone due to trauma, surgical resection, or congenital defects).
requirements.verbatimQuote: Expandable cages are considered medically necessary for members who meet criteria for fusion in CPB 0743 - Spinal Surgery: Laminectomy and Fusion and who meet either of the following criteria: At L2-S1; or For members with osseous defects at the fusion site (i.e., voids or gaps in bone due to trauma, surgical resection, or congenital defects).

exclusions: Interspinous or interlaminar distraction or stabilization devices, with or without lumbar laminectomy and/or fusion, are experimental, investigational, or unproven.
CoFix for interlaminar/interspinous stabilization is experimental, investigational, or unproven.
Expandable cages are experimental, investigational, or unproven for all other indications.
Spine cages and structural allograft are experimental, investigational, or unproven for indications other than interbody fusion.
The Spinal System-X (Corus) is a supply, not an implant, and is covered as part of the global surgical fee - not separately reimbursable.

payers.note: Spine surgery review is delegated to eviCore, which publishes both the criteria and an explicit submission checklist.
payers.accessNotes: FULLY RETRIEVED. 14 guideline PDFs were downloaded directly from evicore.com over HTTPS and text-extracted locally with pdftotext (layout mode, UTF-8). No paywall, no bot-block, no 403. Every quote below was read from the extracted text of the actual PDF. The current effective series is V1.0.2026, Effective Date August 04, 2026 (published April/May 2026) - this is the version in force as of the retrieval date. The superseded V1.0.2025 preface (Effective July 1, 2025) was also retrieved and is recorded separately because it contains one datum the 2026 version dropped: an explicit cotinine cutoff of 10 ng/mL. WHAT IS NOT HERE: (1) eviCore's spine guidelines contain NO ICD-10 code lists - they list CPT codes only, so every icd10Codes array is empty and that is a property of the source, not a gap in retrieval. (2) CPT code tables in these PDFs are two-column layouts that pdftotext de-interleaves incorrectly - the CODE NUMBERS extracted reliably and are recorded, but code-to-description pairings were scrambled in extraction, so descriptions are NOT recorded and codes should be re-verified against the AMA CPT book before billing use. (3) Guidelines retrieved but not fully transcribed into this file: CMM-607 (vertebral augmentation), CMM-612 (grafts), CMM-615 (bone growth stimulation), CMM-616 (vertebral body tethering) - out of scope for adult degenerative spine intake. (4) Within CMM-601/604/613/614 the later repeat-surgery and adjacent-segment subsections were read but only summarized where they simply re-point to earlier sections. (5) No BMI requirement appears anywhere in the spine series - eviCore does not impose one for spine surgery; absence is verified, not assumed. (6) No formal functional-impairment instrument (ODI/NDI) is required - eviCore uses a narrative 'clinically significant functional impairment' standard instead. Character normalization: the degree sign, the greater-than-or-equal sign, and bullet glyphs were confirmed against a second UTF-8 extraction pass and are reproduced faithfully.

requirements.verbatimQuote: Greater than 12 weeks since the prior lumbar decompression

requirements.requirement: POST-OPERATIVE MRI/CT must show the neural compression.
requirements.verbatimQuote: Post-operative MRI/CT shows neural structure compression at the requested level(s) that is concordant with the individual's symptoms and physical exam findings and that is caused by ANY of the following: herniated disc(s) (retained disc material or a recurrent disc herniation) / synovial cyst or arachnoid cyst / central/lateral/foraminal stenosis / osteophytes

requirements.requirement: One of at least TWO required conservative modalities, repeated before revision.
requirements.verbatimQuote: prescription strength analgesics, steroids, gabapentinoids, and/or nonsteroidal anti-inflammatory drugs (NSAIDs) for six (6) weeks

requirements.requirement: One of at least TWO required conservative modalities, repeated before revision.
requirements.verbatimQuote: provider-directed exercise program (prescribed by a physical therapist, chiropractic provider, osteopathic or allopathic physician) for six (6) weeks

requirements.requirement: One of at least TWO required conservative modalities; same level.
requirements.verbatimQuote: epidural steroid injection(s) or selective nerve root block(s) performed at the same level(s) as the requested surgery

procedures.indication: Infection, trauma, tumor, or compression at/behind the vertebral body

requirements.requirement: Corpectomy defined as removal of at least one-third of the lumbar vertebral body; must be performed for one of four listed indications and must be accompanied by fusion.
requirements.verbatimQuote: Complete corpectomy or partial corpectomy (i.e., removal of at least one-third of the vertebral body [not for resection of osteophytes alone]) is performed for ANY of the following: infection / trauma / tumor / compression at or behind the level of the vertebral body

requirements.requirement: Corpectomy must be performed with a lumbar fusion because it creates iatrogenic instability.
requirements.verbatimQuote: Lumbar corpectomy must be performed with a lumbar fusion due to the iatrogenic instability of the corpectomy procedure.

procedures.procedure: Interlaminar decompression device (Coflex) in open lumbar decompression
procedures.indication: Neurogenic claudication or radiculopathy with Meyerding Grade 1 spondylolisthesis

requirements.requirement: Restricted to one or two levels between L1-L5, Meyerding Grade 1 only, open procedure only, and NOT with a fusion at the same level.
requirements.verbatimQuote: The interlaminar decompression device will not be used for an open lumbar decompression performed with a lumbar fusion. / The interlaminar decompression device will only be used at one or two lumbar levels between L1-L5. / Meyerding Grade 1 spondylolisthesis with or without anticipated iatrogenic instability (created by disruption of the posterior elements due to facet joint excision exceeding 50% bilaterally or 75% or more of a single facet during spinal decompression)

exclusions: Coflex is considered not medically necessary when used in ANY of the following scenarios: used without meeting the decompression criteria in the applicable procedure-specific section(s) (initial decompression or repeat decompression) / used in the presence of Meyerding Grade 2 or higher degenerative spondylolisthesis / used in the presence of spondylolysis or isthmic spondylolisthesis / used when a lumbar fusion is also being performed at the same level / used when a lumbar decompression is not performed as an open procedure

requirements.requirement: Must be performed by a spine surgeon holding open-approach privileges at a hospital, HOPD, or ASC.
requirements.verbatimQuote: Endoscopic lumbar decompression requires the procedure be performed by a spine surgeon with surgical privileges at a hospital, hospital outpatient department, or ambulatory surgery center to perform open surgical approach(es) for lumbar decompression.

procedures.indication: Urgent/emergent - conservative care and psych screening waived

requirements.requirement: Any listed urgent/emergent condition waives conservative care, psych screening, and repeat-procedure timing.
requirements.verbatimQuote: Urgent/emergent conditions for lumbar decompression include ANY of the following: acute/unstable traumatic spinal fractures or dislocations with EITHER of the following: neural compression / cerebrospinal fluid (CSF) leak / cauda equina syndrome (CES) / progressive neurological deficit documented on two separate physical exams / neurocompressive pathology with ANY of the following: motor weakness of grade 3/5 or less of specified muscle(s) / rapidly progressive symptoms of motor loss / bowel incontinence / bladder incontinence/retention / epidural hematoma / infection (e.g., discitis, epidural abscess, osteomyelitis) / primary or metastatic neoplastic disease causing pathologic fracture, cord compression, or instability

procedures.procedure: Lumbar fusion with decompression (indirect or direct)

requirements.requirement: Candidate for decompression per CMM-608, PLUS one of the listed imaging instability findings.
requirements.verbatimQuote: The individual is a candidate for lumbar decompression or lumbar corpectomy per CMM-608: Lumbar Decompression.

requirements.requirement: Degenerative spondylolisthesis without spondylolysis requires either >3mm dynamic translation on flexion-extension x-rays (or supine vs upright comparison), or Meyerding Grade II or higher.
requirements.verbatimQuote: degenerative spondylolisthesis without spondylolysis with EITHER of the following: dynamic segmental instability on flexion-extension plain x-rays OR comparison of a supine and upright image, with a difference in translational alignment between vertebrae >3mm between views / Meyerding Grade II or higher spondylolisthesis

requirements.requirement: Spondylolisthesis WITH spondylolysis (isthmic) qualifies under any of four listed x-ray patterns.
requirements.verbatimQuote: spondylolisthesis with spondylolysis (e.g., Isthmic Spondylolisthesis) with ANY of the following: Meyerding Grade I or II spondylolisthesis (anterolisthesis) and plain x-rays support progression of anterolisthesis / Meyerding Grade III or higher spondylolisthesis (anterolisthesis) with 50% anterior slippage OR plain x-rays support progression of anterolisthesis / progressive spinal pain without confirmatory imaging showing progression of spondylolisthesis / multi-level spondylolysis on plain x-rays

requirements.requirement: Other qualifying instability findings: post-op facet-excision instability, pars fracture, or iatrogenic spondylolisthesis from prior decompression. Imaging criteria are waived if instability is found intra-operatively.
requirements.verbatimQuote: post-operative instability created by the disruption of the posterior elements due to facet joint excision that exceeding 50% bilaterally or 75% or more of a single facet / pars fracture / previous spinal decompression that resulted in iatrogenic spondylolisthesis / Criteria exception: When instability is created and/or identified intra-operatively, the above imaging criteria are NOT required.

requirements.requirement: Never-smoker, or 6 weeks nicotine-free validated by objective cotinine testing.
requirements.verbatimQuote: Documentation of nicotine-free status with EITHER of the following: individual is a never-smoker / individual has refrained from smoking, use of smokeless tobacco products, and/or nicotine replacement therapy for at least six (6) weeks prior to planned surgery validated by objective cotinine testing methods (serum, urinary, or saliva) verified as within the normal range for the testing method and lab at which the test was performed

requirements.requirement: Candidate for decompression per CMM-608, plus one of four anticipated-instability scenarios. No pre-op imaging of instability required for this pathway.
requirements.verbatimQuote: Anticipated iatrogenic instability with ANY of the following: created by disruption of the posterior elements due to facet joint excision exceeding 50% bilaterally or 75% or more of a single facet during spinal decompression / created by removal of the pars interarticularis that requires fusion to stabilize / created by decompression for Meyerding Grade I or higher spondylolisthesis with foraminal stenosis / created by complete or partial corpectomy (i.e., removal of at least one-third of the vertebral body [not for resection of osteophytes alone])

requirements.requirement: Never-smoker, or 6 weeks nicotine-free validated by objective cotinine testing.
requirements.verbatimQuote: individual has refrained from smoking, use of smokeless tobacco products, and/or nicotine replacement therapy for at least six (6) weeks prior to planned surgery validated by objective cotinine testing methods (serum, urinary, or saliva) verified as within the normal range for the testing method and lab at which the test was performed

requirements.requirement: Coronal plane deformity OR sagittal imbalance meeting specific numeric thresholds.
requirements.verbatimQuote: Imaging findings include EITHER of the following: coronal plane deformity which includes ANY of the following: Cobb angle >30° / asymmetric disk collapse causing symptomatic foraminal narrowing / global coronal imbalance causing head and trunk shift off the midline / sagittal imbalance which includes ANY of the following: sagittal vertebral axis measurement >8cm / pelvic incidence-lumbar lordosis >15°

requirements.requirement: Never-smoker, or 6 weeks nicotine-free validated by objective cotinine testing.
requirements.verbatimQuote: individual has refrained from smoking, use of smokeless tobacco products, and/or nicotine replacement therapy for at least six (6) weeks prior to planned surgery validated by objective cotinine testing methods (serum, urinary, or saliva) verified as within the normal range for the testing method and lab at which the test was performed

requirements.requirement: Candidate for initial primary discectomy per CMM-606.2, PLUS advanced imaging showing one of three anatomically specific herniation patterns.
requirements.verbatimQuote: Advanced imaging shows ANY of the following: primary extraforaminal disc herniation at L5-S1, in which a far lateral approach is not feasible because of the presence of the iliac wings / primary foraminal disc herniation for which facet resection is necessary to retrieve the disc, which will result in iatrogenic instability / primary disc herniation in the lumbar spine that is at the level of the spinal cord (i.e., low lying conus medullaris)

requirements.requirement: Never-smoker, or 6 weeks nicotine-free validated by objective cotinine testing.
requirements.verbatimQuote: individual has refrained from smoking, use of smokeless tobacco products, and/or nicotine replacement therapy for at least six (6) weeks prior to planned surgery validated by objective cotinine testing methods (serum, urinary, or saliva) verified as within the normal range for the testing method and lab at which the test was performed

requirements.requirement: Candidate for repeat discectomy per CMM-606.3 (which itself requires >12 weeks since the prior microdiscectomy).
requirements.verbatimQuote: The individual is a candidate for repeat lumbar discectomy per CMM 606.3: Repeat Lumbar Microdiscectomy (Laminotomy or Laminectomy) at the Same Level.

requirements.requirement: Anterolisthesis at the requested level demonstrated by >3mm dynamic translation or Meyerding Grade II or higher.
requirements.verbatimQuote: Imaging findings include evidence of anterolisthesis at the requested level(s) that results in EITHER of the following: dynamic segmental instability on flexion-extension plain x-rays OR comparison of a supine and upright image, with a difference in translational alignment between vertebrae >3mm between views / Meyerding Grade II or higher spondylolisthesis

requirements.requirement: Never-smoker, or 6 weeks nicotine-free validated by objective cotinine testing.
requirements.verbatimQuote: individual has refrained from smoking, use of smokeless tobacco products, and/or nicotine replacement therapy for at least six (6) weeks prior to planned surgery validated by objective cotinine testing methods (serum, urinary, or saliva) verified as within the normal range for the testing method and lab at which the test was performed

requirements.requirement: >3mm dynamic translation on flexion-extension x-rays (or supine vs upright), or Meyerding Grade II or higher.
requirements.verbatimQuote: Imaging findings include EITHER of the following at the requested level(s): dynamic segmental instability on flexion-extension plain x-rays OR comparison of a supine and upright image, with a difference in translational alignment between vertebrae >3mm between views / Meyerding Grade II or higher spondylolisthesis

requirements.requirement: Daily significant pain amounting to clinically significant functional impairment.
requirements.verbatimQuote: Symptoms include significant level of pain on a daily basis defined as clinically significant functional impairment (e.g., inability to perform household chores, prolonged standing, etc.)

requirements.requirement: THREE consecutive months minimum - note this is longer than the 6 weeks required for decompression. Either medication OR provider-directed exercise satisfies it.
requirements.verbatimQuote: Less than clinically meaningful improvement with EITHER of the following (unless contraindicated) for at least three (3) consecutive months: prescription strength analgesics, steroids, gabapentinoids, and/or nonsteroidal anti-inflammatory drugs (NSAIDs)

requirements.requirement: THREE consecutive months minimum, as the alternative to the medication trial.
requirements.verbatimQuote: provider-directed exercise program (prescribed by a physical therapist, chiropractic provider, osteopathic or allopathic physician)

requirements.requirement: Negative attestation for unmanaged mental/behavioral health disorders.
requirements.verbatimQuote: Absence of unmanaged significant mental and/or behavioral health disorders (e.g., major depressive disorder, chronic pain syndrome, secondary gain, opioid and alcohol use disorders)

requirements.requirement: Never-smoker, or 6 weeks nicotine-free validated by objective cotinine testing.
requirements.verbatimQuote: individual has refrained from smoking, use of smokeless tobacco products, and/or nicotine replacement therapy for at least six (6) weeks prior to planned surgery validated by objective cotinine testing methods (serum, urinary, or saliva) verified as within the normal range for the testing method and lab at which the test was performed

requirements.requirement: Any of four plain-x-ray patterns at the requested level.
requirements.verbatimQuote: Imaging findings include ANY of the following at the requested level(s): Meyerding Grade I or II spondylolisthesis (anterolisthesis) and plain x-rays support progression of anterolisthesis / Meyerding Grade III or higher spondylolisthesis (anterolisthesis) with 50% anterior slippage OR plain x-rays support progression of anterolisthesis / progressive spinal pain without confirmatory imaging showing progression of spondylolisthesis / multi-level spondylolysis on plain x-rays

requirements.requirement: Daily significant pain amounting to clinically significant functional impairment.
requirements.verbatimQuote: Symptoms include significant level of pain on a daily basis defined as clinically significant functional impairment (e.g., inability to perform household chores, prolonged standing, etc.)

requirements.requirement: THREE consecutive months minimum; medication or provider-directed exercise.
requirements.verbatimQuote: Less than clinically meaningful improvement with EITHER of the following (unless contraindicated) for at least three (3) consecutive months: prescription strength analgesics, steroids, gabapentinoids, and/or nonsteroidal anti-inflammatory drugs (NSAIDs)

requirements.requirement: THREE consecutive months minimum.
requirements.verbatimQuote: provider-directed exercise program (prescribed by a physical therapist, chiropractic provider, osteopathic or allopathic physician)

requirements.requirement: Never-smoker, or 6 weeks nicotine-free validated by objective cotinine testing.
requirements.verbatimQuote: individual has refrained from smoking, use of smokeless tobacco products, and/or nicotine replacement therapy for at least six (6) weeks prior to planned surgery validated by objective cotinine testing methods (serum, urinary, or saliva) verified as within the normal range for the testing method and lab at which the test was performed

procedures.indication: Discogenic lower back pain / degenerative disc disease

requirements.requirement: BOTH plain x-rays AND advanced imaging (CT or MRI) must show moderate-to-severe SINGLE-LEVEL disc degeneration at the requested level.
requirements.verbatimQuote: Plain x-rays and advanced imaging (i.e., CT, MRI) show moderate to severe single-level disc degeneration at the requested level(s).

requirements.requirement: Chronic unremitting discogenic axial low back pain and associated disability for at least ONE YEAR. This is the longest symptom-duration requirement in the lumbar series.
requirements.verbatimQuote: Presence of chronic, unremitting, discogenic axial lower back pain and associated disability secondary to single-level degenerative lumbar disc disease (DDD) for at least one year

requirements.requirement: Daily significant pain amounting to clinically significant functional impairment.
requirements.verbatimQuote: Symptoms include significant level of pain on a daily basis defined as clinically significant functional impairment (e.g., inability to perform household chores, prolonged standing, etc.)

requirements.requirement: Requires a STRUCTURED physician-supervised multi-modal nonoperative program with regularly scheduled appointments and follow-up evaluation - and, if the exercise program is one of the two chosen modalities, TWELVE consecutive months of it.
requirements.verbatimQuote: Structured physician-supervised, multi-modal, nonoperative management of medical care with licensed healthcare professionals which includes ALL of the following: regularly scheduled appointments / follow-up evaluation / less than clinically meaningful improvement with at least TWO of the following (unless contraindicated): ... provider-directed exercise program (prescribed by a physical therapist, chiropractic provider, osteopathic or allopathic physician) for at least 12 consecutive months

requirements.requirement: TWELVE consecutive months of prescription-strength medication, as one of at least TWO required modalities.
requirements.verbatimQuote: prescription strength analgesics, steroids, gabapentinoids, and/or nonsteroidal anti-inflammatory drugs (NSAIDs) for at least 12 consecutive months

requirements.requirement: ESI or SNRB at the same level counts as one of the two required modalities; no duration specified.
requirements.verbatimQuote: epidural steroid injection(s) or selective nerve root block(s) performed at the same level(s) as the requested surgery

requirements.requirement: Facet joint injections or medial branch blocks count as one of the two required modalities.
requirements.verbatimQuote: facet joint injection(s)/medial branch block(s)/radiofrequency ablation(s)

requirements.requirement: Radiofrequency ablation counts as one of the two required modalities.
requirements.verbatimQuote: facet joint injection(s)/medial branch block(s)/radiofrequency ablation(s)

requirements.requirement: Negative attestation for unmanaged mental/behavioral health disorders.
requirements.verbatimQuote: Absence of unmanaged significant mental and/or behavioral health disorders (e.g., major depressive disorder, chronic pain syndrome, secondary gain, opioid and alcohol use disorders)

requirements.requirement: Never-smoker, or 6 weeks nicotine-free validated by objective cotinine testing.
requirements.verbatimQuote: individual has refrained from smoking, use of smokeless tobacco products, and/or nicotine replacement therapy for at least six (6) weeks prior to planned surgery validated by objective cotinine testing methods (serum, urinary, or saliva) verified as within the normal range for the testing method and lab at which the test was performed

procedures.procedure: Lumbar fusion (arthrodesis) for adjacent segment disease

requirements.requirement: The prior adjacent-level lumbar fusion must have been performed at least 6 months before, AND the applicable 609.4 or 609.5 criteria must also be met in full.
requirements.verbatimQuote: The prior adjacent-level lumbar fusion was performed at least 6 months prior

procedures.procedure: Repeat lumbar fusion (arthrodesis) at the same level

requirements.requirement: More than 6 months since the prior lumbar fusion.
requirements.verbatimQuote: Greater than six (6) months since the prior lumbar fusion

requirements.requirement: Post-operative imaging performed NO EARLIER than 6 months after the prior fusion must show pseudoarthrosis at the requested level, and post-op MRI/CT findings must be concordant with symptoms.
requirements.durationRequired: no less than six (6) months after the prior lumbar fusion
requirements.verbatimQuote: Post-operative imaging (performed at no less than six (6) months after the prior lumbar fusion) shows pseudoarthrosis at the requested level(s)

requirements.requirement: BOTH medication and exercise required (not 'either') - 6 weeks each.
requirements.verbatimQuote: Less than clinically meaningful improvement with BOTH of the following (unless contraindicated): prescription strength analgesics, steroids, gabapentinoids, and/or nonsteroidal anti-inflammatory drugs (NSAIDs) for six (6) weeks

requirements.requirement: BOTH medication and exercise required - 6 weeks each.
requirements.verbatimQuote: provider-directed exercise program (prescribed by a physical therapist, chiropractic provider, osteopathic or allopathic physician) for six (6) weeks

requirements.requirement: Daily significant pain with functional impairment, and post-op exam findings concordant with symptoms.
requirements.verbatimQuote: Post-operative physical exam findings are concordant with the individual's symptoms

requirements.requirement: Never-smoker, or 6 weeks nicotine-free validated by objective cotinine testing.
requirements.verbatimQuote: individual has refrained from smoking, use of smokeless tobacco products, and/or nicotine replacement therapy for at least six (6) weeks prior to planned surgery validated by objective cotinine testing methods (serum, urinary, or saliva) verified as within the normal range for the testing method and lab at which the test was performed

procedures.procedure: Lumbar fusion following failed lumbar disc arthroplasty
procedures.indication: Failed implant, or neural compression after arthroplasty

requirements.requirement: Failed implant pathway requires post-op imaging showing malposition or failure. The neural-compression pathway requires >6 months since the arthroplasty plus post-op MRI/CT showing compression, plus full 609.4 or 609.5 criteria.
requirements.verbatimQuote: Post-operative imaging shows evidence of lumbar disc arthroplasty implant malposition or failure (e.g., subsidence, loosening, infection, dislocation, subluxation, vertebral body fracture, dislodgement)

requirements.requirement: For the neural-compression pathway, more than 6 months must have elapsed since the prior lumbar total disc arthroplasty at the same level.
requirements.verbatimQuote: Greater than six (6) months since the prior lumbar total disc arthroplasty at the same level

procedures.indication: Urgent/emergent - conservative care, smoking cessation, psych screening all waived

requirements.requirement: Any listed urgent/emergent condition waives conservative care, proof of smoking cessation, psych screening, and repeat-procedure timing.
requirements.verbatimQuote: Urgent/emergent conditions for lumbar fusion and/or osteotomy include ANY of the following: traumatic spinal fractures or dislocations (with or without neural compression) when instability is present or decompression of the spinal canal is anticipated to result in iatrogenic instability / infection (e.g., discitis, epidural abscess, osteomyelitis) when instability is present or debridement and/or decompression is anticipated to result in iatrogenic instability / primary or metastatic neoplastic disease causing pathologic fracture, cord compression, when instability is present, or resection and/or decompression is anticipated to result in iatrogenic instability / a condition otherwise meeting criteria listed in the applicable procedure section(s) with documentation of severe debilitating pain and/or dysfunction to the point of being incapacitated

requirements.requirement: Posterior column osteotomy requires non-fixed deformity needing 5-10 degrees correction per segment with SVA >8cm or PI-LL >15 degrees, or limited-flexibility coronal deformity with Cobb >30 degrees. Maximum four PCOs per correction surgery (no limit for Scheuermann's kyphosis).
requirements.verbatimQuote: Performed for non-fixed deformity requiring 5° to 10° of correction (SPO) per spinal segment with EITHER of the following: lumbar sagittal plane deformities where sagittal vertical axis (SVA) is >8cm or pelvic incidence-lumbar lordosis (PI-LL) is >15° / larger coronal deformities where there is limited flexibility and the Cobb angle is >30° ... Posterior column osteotomy is limited to a maximum of four (4) posterior column osteotomies performed in the apex of the deformity per correction surgery.

requirements.requirement: Three-column osteotomy (PSO or VCR) requires fixed sagittal deformity needing >30 degrees correction, or large fixed coronal deformity >60 degrees amenable to asymmetric osteotomy.
requirements.verbatimQuote: Performed for EITHER of the following: fixed sagittal plane deformity requiring >30° of correction (PSO) / large, fixed coronal deformities >60° that are amenable to asymmetric osteotomy

procedures.procedure: Initial primary lumbar total disc arthroplasty

requirements.requirement: Age 18-60. Single level only, at L3-L4, L4-L5, or L5-S1. No planned simultaneous adjacent-level fusion. No facet ankylosis or severe facet degeneration at the operative level.
requirements.verbatimQuote: Age is 18-60 years / Lumbar disc prosthesis is approved by the FDA or for an FDA approved indication and in accordance with FDA labeling / No planned simultaneous fusion (hybrid surgery) at an adjacent lumbar level / The planned implant will be used in the reconstruction of a single-level lumbar disc at only one of the following lumbar levels: L3-4, L4-L5, or L5-S1 / Absence of facet ankylosis or severe facet degeneration at the operative level

requirements.requirement: Plain x-rays AND advanced imaging (CT, MRI) must confirm moderate-to-severe single-level degeneration at the operative level, absence of DDD above L3-L4, and absence of DDD at more than one level.
requirements.verbatimQuote: Plain x-rays and advanced diagnostic imaging studies (i.e., CT, MRI) confirm ALL of the following: presence of moderate to severe single-level disc degeneration at the operative level (between L3-L4, L4-L5, or L5-S1) / absence of degenerative disc disease above L3-L4 / absence of degenerative disc disease at more than one level (between L3-L4, L4-L5, or L5-S1)

requirements.requirement: Plain x-rays required in addition to advanced imaging.
requirements.verbatimQuote: Plain x-rays and advanced diagnostic imaging studies (i.e., CT, MRI) confirm ALL of the following

requirements.requirement: SIX consecutive months. BOTH medication and provider-directed exercise are required (not either/or), within a structured physician-supervised program.
requirements.verbatimQuote: Structured physician-supervised, multi-modal, nonoperative management of medical care with licensed healthcare professionals which includes ALL of the following: regularly scheduled appointments / follow-up evaluation / less than clinically meaningful improvement with BOTH of the following (unless contraindicated) for at least six (6) consecutive months: prescription strength analgesics, steroids, gabapentinoids, and/or nonsteroidal anti-inflammatory drugs (NSAIDs) / provider-directed exercise program (prescribed by a physical therapist, chiropractic provider, osteopathic or allopathic physician)

requirements.requirement: SIX consecutive months of provider-directed exercise, required alongside the medication trial.
requirements.verbatimQuote: provider-directed exercise program (prescribed by a physical therapist, chiropractic provider, osteopathic or allopathic physician)

requirements.requirement: Osteopenia or osteoporosis with T-score below -1.0 is an absolute contraindication - this makes DEXA effectively mandatory where bone quality is in question.
requirements.verbatimQuote: the individual has osteopenia or osteoporosis (T-score < -1.0)

requirements.requirement: Negative attestation for unmanaged mental/behavioral health disorders.
requirements.verbatimQuote: Absence of unmanaged significant mental and/or behavioral health disorders (e.g., major depressive disorder, chronic pain syndrome, secondary gain, opioid and alcohol use disorders)

exclusions: Lumbar total disc arthroplasty is considered not medically necessary when performed using lumbar partial disc prosthetics.
Lumbar total disc arthroplasty is considered not medically necessary when performed as an adjunct to the treatment of primary-central or far-lateral disc herniation.

Contraindications making it not medically necessary: performed for the revision of a failed lumbar artificial total disc arthroplasty / the individual has osteopenia or osteoporosis (T-score < -1.0) / imaging evidence of ANY of the following: degenerative or lytic spondylolisthesis >3mm / lumbar spinal stenosis / pars interarticularis defect with either spondylolysis or isthmic spondylolisthesis / lumbar scoliosis (>11° of sagittal plane deformity) / spinal fracture / infection / presence of tumor or active infection at the site of implantation / lumbar nerve root compression or bony spinal stenosis / preoperative remaining disc height <3mm / mid-sagittal stenosis of <8mm (by MRI)

history of ankylosing spondylitis, rheumatoid arthritis, lupus, or other autoimmune disorder / allergy or sensitivity to implant materials / isolated radicular compression syndromes especially due to lumbar disc herniation / involved vertebral endplate is dimensionally smaller than the approximate dimensions of the implant in anterior/posterior width and lateral width / clinically compromised vertebral bodies at the affected level due to current or past trauma

procedures.procedure: Minimally invasive sacroiliac joint fusion and stabilization
procedures.indication: Lumbopelvic pain originating from the SI joint

requirements.requirement: TWO separate diagnostic SI joint injections, each with a positive response defined as 75% pain reduction for the duration of the local anesthetic.
requirements.verbatimQuote: Diagnostic confirmation of the SI joint as a pain generator as evidenced by a positive response to two separate diagnostic SI joint injections. A positive response to a diagnostic SI joint injection is considered 75% reduction in the reported pain for the duration of the local anesthetic.

requirements.requirement: Separately from the two diagnostic injections, a trial of at least ONE therapeutic SI joint injection with less than clinically meaningful improvement.
requirements.verbatimQuote: a trial of at least one (1) therapeutic SI joint injection

requirements.requirement: Plain x-rays and/or CT/MRI to exclude destructive lesions and acute fracture/instability; PLUS plain x-rays of the pelvis including the ipsilateral hip to evaluate concomitant hip pathology.
requirements.verbatimQuote: plain x-rays and/or cross-sectional imaging (CT or MRI) have been performed to exclude the presence of ANY of the following that would not be properly addressed by SIJ fusion: destructive lesions (e.g., tumor, infection) / acute traumatic fracture and/or instability of the SI joint / plain x-rays of the pelvis (including the ipsilateral hip) have been performed to evaluate potential concomitant hip pathology as a potential more likely source for the individual's pain

requirements.requirement: Cross-sectional imaging (CT or MRI) of the LUMBAR SPINE is separately required, to rule out neural compression as a more likely pain source.
requirements.verbatimQuote: cross-sectional imaging (e.g., CT or MRI) of the lumbar spine have been performed to evaluate potential concomitant neural compression or other degenerative conditions as a potential more likely source for the individual's pain

requirements.requirement: ALL THREE symptom criteria required: Fortin's point localization, non-radiating lumbopelvic pain caudal to L5, and interference with ADLs.
requirements.verbatimQuote: Symptoms include ALL of the following: individual localizes posterior pain to the posterior superior iliac spine (Fortin's point) / presence of non-radiating lumbopelvic pain caudal to L5, buttock, hip, and/or groin pain / SI joint pain interfering with activities of daily living

requirements.requirement: ALL exam criteria required, including reproduction of SI pain on at least THREE of seven named provocative tests.
requirements.verbatimQuote: Physical exam findings include ALL of the following: localized tenderness to palpation over the sacral sulcus and posterior SI joint / absence of localized tenderness (of similar severity to palpation of the sacral sulcus and posterior SI joint) over the greater trochanter, lumbar spine, and coccyx / reproduction of localized sacroiliac joint pain on at least three (3) of the following provocative tests: thigh thrust test (posterior pelvic pain provocational test) / sacroiliac joint compression test / Gaenslen's test / distraction test (gapping test) / FABER test (Patrick's test) / sacral thrust test / Yeoman's test

requirements.requirement: SIX consecutive months of NSAIDs, AND separately six consecutive months of prescription medication optimization. All four conservative modalities are required (ALL, not 'at least two').
requirements.verbatimQuote: Less than clinically meaningful improvement with ALL of the following (unless contraindicated): ... non-steroidal anti-inflammatory drugs (NSAIDs) for at least six (6) consecutive months / prescription medication optimization for at least six (6) consecutive months

requirements.requirement: SIX consecutive months of physician supervised/prescribed ACTIVE physical therapy targeting the lumbopelvic (core) area. Chiropractic is explicitly NOT a substitute.
requirements.verbatimQuote: physician supervised/prescribed active physical therapy (including home exercise program) targeting lumbopelvic (core) area for at least six (6) consecutive months. Note: Chiropractic adjustments may be performed as an additional treatment option, but chiropractic adjustments are NOT required and are NOT considered a substitute for physical therapy.

requirements.requirement: A home exercise program is explicitly included within the required six months of active physical therapy.
requirements.verbatimQuote: physician supervised/prescribed active physical therapy (including home exercise program) targeting lumbopelvic (core) area for at least six (6) consecutive months

requirements.requirement: Chiropractic adjustments are optional and explicitly do NOT substitute for the required physical therapy.
requirements.verbatimQuote: Note: Chiropractic adjustments may be performed as an additional treatment option, but chiropractic adjustments are NOT required and are NOT considered a substitute for physical therapy.

requirements.requirement: Absence of generalized pain behavior or generalized pain disorders (e.g., fibromyalgia), AND absence of unmanaged mental/behavioral health disorders.

Epidural corticosteroid injection(s) count as the complementary conservative treatment. NOT independently mandatory anywhere in this guideline.
Chiropractic manipulation counts as an alternative-therapy complementary conservative treatment.
Acupuncture counts as an alternative-therapy complementary conservative treatment.
Operational definition of significant pain: at least 3 out of 10.
Operational definition of significant functional impairment: inability to perform at least two ADLs and/or IADLs.
All imaging must be performed and read by an independent radiologist and must correlate with clinical findings.

Failure of conservative management requires a completed full course for the current episode of care, worsening or no significant improvement on clinical reevaluation, and consideration of more invasive therapy.
STRONGLY RECOMMENDED, not a hard requirement: tobacco abstinence for at least 6 weeks pre-op.
